Quote.body: Government of the people, by the people, for the people, shall not perish from the earth.
Quote.author: Abraham Lincoln

Quote.body: Always bear in mind that your own resolution to succeed is more important than any other.
Quote.author: Abraham Lincoln

Quote.body: Nearly all men can stand adversity, but if you want to test a man's character, give him power.
Quote.author: Abraham Lincoln

Quote.body: Far and away the best prize that life offers is the chance to work hard at work worth doing.
Quote.author: Theodore Roosevelt

Quote.body: People ask the difference between a leader and a boss. The leader leads, and the boss drives.
Quote.author: Theodore Roosevelt

Quote.body: Success is not final, failure is not fatal: it is the courage to continue that counts.
Quote.author: Winston Churchill

Quote.body: The greatest glory in living lies not in never falling, but in rising every time we fall.
Quote.author: Nelson Mandela

Quote.body: Leadership is the art of getting someone else to do something you want done because he wants to do it.
Quote.author: Dwight D. Eisenhower

Quote.body: If your actions inspire others to dream more, learn more, do more and become more, you are a leader.
Quote.author: John Quincy Adams

Quote.body: There are no secrets to success. It is the result of preparation, hard work, and learning from failure.
Quote.author: Colin Powell

Quote.body: When you arise in the morning, think of what a precious privilege it is to be alive.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: Look well into thyself; there is a source of strength which will always spring up.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: If anyone tells you that a certain person speaks ill of you, do not make excuses.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: No person has the power to have everything they want, but in their power is not to want what they do not have.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: True happiness is to enjoy the present, without anxious dependence upon the future.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: If you are distressed by anything external, the pain is not due to the thing itself.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: No one can lose either the past or the future - how could anyone be deprived of what he does not possess?
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: If someone is able to show me that what I think or do is not right, I will happily change.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: Freedom is secured not by the fulfilling of desires, but by the removal of desire.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: You have power over your mind - not outside events.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: To lose one parent may be regarded as a misfortune; to lose both looks like carelessness.
Quote.author: Oscar Wilde
Quote.attribution: The Importance of Being Earnest (1895) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Oscar_Wilde

Quote.body: I never travel without my diary. One should always have something sensational to read in the train.
Quote.author: Oscar Wilde
Quote.attribution: The Importance of Being Earnest (1895) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Oscar_Wilde

Quote.body: I find television very educational. Every time someone switches it on I go into another room and read a good book.
Quote.author: Groucho Marx

Quote.body: Although it is generally known, I think it is about time to announce that I was born at a very early age.
Quote.author: Groucho Marx

Quote.body: I am so clever that sometimes I don't understand a single word of what I am saying.
Quote.author: Oscar Wilde
Quote.attribution: The Happy Prince preface attribution | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Oscar_Wilde

Quote.body: A common mistake that people make when trying to design something completely foolproof is to underestimate the ingenuity of complete fools.
Quote.author: Douglas Adams

Quote.body: Outside of a dog, a book is man's best friend. Inside of a dog it's too dark to read.
Quote.author: Groucho Marx

Quote.body: I don't deserve this award, but I have arthritis and I don't deserve that either.
Quote.author: Jack Benny

Quote.body: Never put off till tomorrow what you can do the day after tomorrow just as well.
Quote.author: Mark Twain

Quote.body: My ability to turn good news into anxiety is rivaled only by my ability to turn anxiety into chin acne.
Quote.author: Tina Fey

Quote.body: Of all the means to insure happiness throughout the whole life, friendship is most important.
Quote.author: Epicurus

Quote.body: What you leave behind is not what is engraved in stone monuments, but what is woven into the lives of others.
Quote.author: Pericles

Quote.body: The greatest way to live with honor in this world is to be what we pretend to be.
Quote.author: Socrates

Quote.body: Courage is the first of human qualities because it is the quality which guarantees all others.
Quote.author: Aristotle

Quote.body: Music gives a soul to the universe, wings to the mind, flight to the imagination.
Quote.author: Plato

Quote.body: He who learns but does not think is lost; he who thinks but does not learn is in danger.
Quote.author: Attributed in classical anthologies

Quote.body: The unexamined life is not worth living.
Quote.author: Socrates

Quote.body: I know that I know nothing.
Quote.author: Socrates

Quote.body: The only true wisdom is in knowing you know nothing.
Quote.author: Socrates

Quote.body: Be as you wish to seem.
Quote.author: Socrates

Quote.body: When government violates the rights of the people, insurrection is a sacred right and duty.
Quote.author: French National Convention

Quote.body: The free communication of ideas and opinions is one of the most precious rights of man.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 11 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: All citizens are equally eligible to all dignities, places and public employments.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 6 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: Property being an inviolable and sacred right, no one shall be deprived thereof except where public necessity demands.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 17 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: A society in which rights are not secured nor separation of powers established has no constitution.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 16 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: No one shall be disquieted on account of his opinions, including religious views.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 10 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: A common contribution is essential for maintenance of the public force and administration.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 13 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: Citizens have the right to verify the necessity of public taxation and to monitor its use.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 14 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: Society has the right to require every public agent to account for his administration.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 15 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: The social aim of all political institutions is the preservation of the natural rights of man.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
